info.title: Paprel Public API
info.description:
External gateway API. Access requires the documented token audience and permissions.

## Integration conventions

### Request headers
* `x-partner-domain` is required where the operation declares it as a required header. It is optional but recommended on `POST /v1/app-connect/oauth/token`: the token exchange can resolve the partner from the client’s company. The `/partner/*` operations resolve the partner from credentials or the partner token and do not use this header. OAuth discovery and other explicitly exempt operations also do not require it. On operations that require it, omission is rejected with HTTP 400 and `Missing required x-partner-domain header`. A domain that is not registered returns HTTP 404 `PARTNER_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED`, which deliberately does not say whether the domain exists.
* Send an identifying `User-Agent`. Default library agents (for example the stock Python `urllib` one) can be blocked at the edge with `error code: 1010`, which looks like an authentication failure.

### Request examples
* Example UUIDs and credentials are fictional. Replace record IDs with IDs from your own company, use an open accounting date, and choose the company base currency or supply the required exchange rate.

### Workflow inputs

| Task | What to send | Where to find it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Find accounts for items, payments and journals | Account `id` values, looked up by `account_code` (for example `sales_revenue`, `operating_cash`, `capital`). | `GET /v1/accounting/accounts` for the company. |
| Create an item | `item_type`: `goods` or `service`. Only these two values are accepted. | Choose the value that describes the item. |
| Send an invoice | `to_state` in `PUT /v1/invoices/{id}/state-transition`; in the default workflow, use `sent` from `draft`. | `GET /v1/invoices/setting/state-transition` lists each `from_state` and its allowed `to_state` values; use the company's configured transitions. |
| Record a payment: deposit account | `deposit_account`: the `id` of an asset account from the chart, for example operating cash. | `GET /v1/accounting/accounts`. A new company has no bank accounts, so `GET /v1/accounting/bank-accounts` returns an empty list until bank accounts are added. |
| Record a payment: payment mode | `payment_mode`: a label such as `Bank Transfer`, `Cash` or `Credit Card`. | `GET /v1/company/payment-modes` lists the company's labels. |
| Retry a payment safely | Reuse the same `Idempotency-Key` header and an identical body, including `payment_date`. | A matching retry returns the saved payment; changed payment details under the same key are refused with HTTP 409. |

### Responses
* Successful responses carry the payload under `data`; error responses are top level. The OAuth token endpoint (`POST /app-connect/oauth/token`) is the exception: it returns the standard RFC 6749 token response, so read `access_token` from the top level.
* Most list endpoints are page-numbered: `page` (1-based) and `page_size` (1 to 200, default 50; larger values return 200). The response repeats `page_number`, `page_size` and `total_records`; walk pages until you have `total_records` rows. A few lists name these differently and say so on the operation (custom FX rates use `page_number`; webhook deliveries use `per_page`, at most 100). Dimensions, the dimension worklist and the activity feed are cursor-paged: pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` with the same filters. Unknown query parameters are ignored, not rejected. List envelopes use different keys per module (for example `peoples`, `items`, `docs`, `accounts`).

### Access tokens
* App Connect access tokens expire after `expires_in` seconds (one hour by default). Request a new token when yours expires; the same client may be handed the same token until it nears expiry.

### Rate limits
* Rate-limited operations document their limit on their `429` response: requests per minute per client, and the burst allowed. Payment and other money-movement operations (recording or deleting a payment, applying credits, online payment, bulk payments) allow 20 requests per minute (burst of 25); imports, mail sends and other heavy writes 6; reports 12.
* A `429` has no body and no `Retry-After` header. Wait 60 divided by the per-minute limit, in seconds, before the next call (3 seconds at 20 per minute). A `503` with no body means the operation's shared limit across all clients was reached; retry with backoff.
* To record many payments, `POST /invoices/payments/bulk` records full payments for a list of invoices that share one payment mode, date and deposit account in a single call; payments that differ in date, mode or amount still need one call each. Prefer other bulk variants too (for example `PUT /invoices/state-transition/bulk`).

### Document lifecycle and posting
* New invoices, bills and expenses are created as `draft`. A draft has not reached a posting transition, so it is not in the ledger, receivables or payables.
* Move invoices and bills forward with their `state-transition` operations, and expenses with `POST /expenses/state-transition` (`draft` -> `submitted` -> `approved`).
* Which transition posts the ledger entry is set per company on the status transitions (see the `/state-transition/ledger-effects` operations). In the default workflow an invoice posts when it is marked `sent`, and a bill or expense when it is `approved`.

get.description:
Returns a comprehensive, flat-mapped registry of the organization's accounts. While this endpoint does not return a nested tree structure, each record includes its primary classification (Asset, Liability, etc.) and relational metadata (Parent ID), making it ideal for high-performance search, filtering, and data-table rendering.

The API Gateway requires a bearer access token. Required permissions (any): accounting:account-add, accounting:account-list, accounting:account-edit, role:admin. Audience and session binding checks also apply. A browser session route is not automatically available to partner credentials. Provide only the documented query parameters; tenant context is determined by authentication and the requested operation.

401.description: Unauthorized: JWT Bearer token missing or expired.

500.description: Internal Server Error: An unexpected error occurred on the server. The body is either the JSON string `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` or the standard `{"error": {code, message}}` envelope, depending on the route.

post.description:
Adds a new account definition to the organization's financial registry. This process assigns the account to a specific classification (Asset, Liability, Equity, etc.) and establishes its position within the ledger hierarchy. Once created, the account becomes available for journal entries and financial reporting.

The API Gateway requires a bearer access token. Required permissions (any): accounting:account-add, role:admin. Audience and session binding checks also apply. A browser session route is not automatically available to partner credentials.

200.description: Account successfully registered and activated in the ledger

400.description: Validation failed for one or more fields, or a business rule rejected the request. Field validation returns `{"error": {field: [codes]}}`; other rejections return `{"error": {code, message, details?}}`.

Updates the metadata and classification logic for an existing account subtype. This action allows for the refinement of financial reporting categories without needing to reclassify individual accounts. **Note:** Updating a subtype's primary mapping will immediately reflect across all linked accounts in the Chart of Accounts and on generated financial statements.

The API Gateway requires a bearer access token. Required permissions (any): accounting:account-add, accounting:account-edit, role:admin. Audience and session binding checks also apply. A browser session route is not automatically available to partner credentials.

Provides a detailed view of a specific account, including its configuration metadata and real-time financial statistics. This view aggregates current balances, last activity dates, and period-over-period performance metrics, serving as the primary data source for Account Detail 'White Cards' in the dashboard.

put.description:
Updates the configuration of an existing account in the Chart of Accounts. Use this to adjust the account name, internal code, or re-parent it within the ledger hierarchy. **Note:** Changing an account's primary classification (e.g., Asset to Expense) is restricted if the account contains existing journal entries to prevent ledger corruption.

The API Gateway requires a bearer access token. Required permissions (any): accounting:account-add, accounting:account-edit, role:admin. Audience and session binding checks also apply. A browser session route is not automatically available to partner credentials.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the account to modify

delete.description:
Permanent removal of an account from the Chart of Accounts. **Safety Restriction:** An account can only be deleted if it has a zero balance and no historical journal entries. If the account has transaction history, consider deactivating it via the Update endpoint instead to preserve the audit trail.

The API Gateway requires a bearer access token. Required permissions (any): accounting:account-delete, role:admin. Audience and session binding checks also apply. A browser session route is not automatically available to partner credentials. Provide only the documented query parameters; tenant context is determined by authentication and the requested operation.

get.summary: List posted records with missing dimensions
get.description:
Posted records that have taggable revenue/expense lines without a value for at least one dimension, newest first, one row per record. module is documents (with doc_type invoice, bill or credit-note), expenses or journals (manual journals). Cursor-paged. The API Gateway checks the income-statement report permission (or role:admin). The backend additionally enforces the requested owner's list permission: invoice:list, bill:list, credit-note:list, expense:list, or accounting:journal-list. The x-api-gateway-auth metadata describes gateway checks only.

The API Gateway requires a bearer access token. Required permissions (any): report:income-statement, role:admin. Audience and session binding checks also apply. A browser session route is not automatically available to partner credentials.

parameters.description: `documents`, `expenses` or `journals`.

parameters.description: `invoice`, `bill` or `credit-note`; required for `documents`, rejected otherwise.

parameters.description: Required, `YYYY-MM-DD,YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive, at most 366 days.

put.description:
Changes the dimension values of an issued document's lines and nothing else (amounts, accounts, taxes and dates cannot be sent). Each listed line gets exactly the values sent (an empty list clears it); lines not listed keep theirs. The document's current version is updated in place and its journal re-posted with the new resolved values. Send expected_version (the current version_number). Transaction Locking applies as for an edit: a hard lock refuses the call, a soft lock lets a user with the bypass permission through and is logged.

The API Gateway requires a bearer access token. Required permissions (any): invoice:edit, role:admin. Audience and session binding checks also apply. A browser session route is not automatically available to partner credentials.

get.description:
Retrieves the exchange rate `1 base = rate target` between two ISO-4217 currencies. For an authenticated company, a custom FX window covering `at` (default now) takes precedence when the pair includes the company base currency (`source = custom`); otherwise the real-time or cached provider rate is returned (`source = automatic`). This is the primary endpoint for calculating transaction totals and tax liabilities in multi-currency environments.

The API Gateway requires a bearer access token.

Moment to resolve the rate for: `YYYY-MM-DD` (a company-local date, e.g. a
document issue date) or an RFC 3339 timestamp. Defaults to now. Only selects the
company custom FX window; the automatic fallback is always the latest provider rate.

post.description:
Resolves up to 500 `1 base = rate target` lookups in one call, each for its own transaction date `at` (`YYYY-MM-DD` company-local, or RFC 3339; default today). Same rules as `GET /settings/currency-rate`: for an authenticated company a custom FX window covering the date wins when the pair includes the company base currency (`source = custom`), otherwise the provider rate (`source = automatic`). Automatic rates are the latest stored rate; `as_of_date_matched = false` flags an automatic rate returned for a past date. Items that cannot be resolved come back with `rate = null` and `error = RATE_NOT_FOUND`; malformed items fail the whole request with 400.

The API Gateway requires a bearer access token.

put.description:
Sets how many companies the caller's organization pays for on the Standard plan, the organization included. Call it as the organization company, with `company:subscription`. An increase is invoiced at once and charged to the saved card, prorated to the next billing date, and applied only after payment. For API callers, if the card requires authentication or payment is declined, no update remains pending and the call answers 402 `COMPANY_QUANTITY_PAYMENT_ACTION_REQUIRED` with `message` and `subscription_url`, the web app's Subscription page. Open Subscription in the web app to finish the change. Web callers can receive 202 with a Stripe-hosted payment URL. The increase remains pending until paid or expired, and other changes are blocked in the meantime. A decrease applies at once; the unused time on the removed companies becomes account credit for the next invoices and is never paid out. Send back the `proration_date` a preview returned to charge exactly what was previewed. When Stripe's answer is lost, or Core could not record an applied change, the call answers 202 with `pending_company_quantity` and `pending_change_id`; Core then reads Stripe (never resends) and settles the change when Stripe shows the requested count. An unresolved change can require operator review. While a change is open, another answers 409 `COMPANY_QUANTITY_CHANGE_IN_PROGRESS`. Refused with 409 `COMPANY_QUANTITY_BELOW_IN_USE` below the companies in use, 409 `COMPANY_QUANTITY_INCREASE_TOO_LARGE` when one change adds more than `max_increase` companies (50 by default; raise the count in steps), 409 `COMPANY_QUANTITY_SET_AT_CHECKOUT` during the trial, 409 `SUBSCRIPTION_CANCEL_PENDING` while the plan is set to end, 409 `ORGANIZATION_PLAN_INACTIVE` or `ORGANIZATION_PLAN_REQUIRED` without a live Standard plan, 409 `SUBSCRIPTION_MANAGED_BY_ORGANIZATION` when called as a member company, and 502 `COMPANY_QUANTITY_UPDATE_REFUSED` when Stripe refuses the change for another reason.

The API Gateway requires a bearer access token. Required permissions (any): company:subscription, role:admin. Audience and session binding checks also apply. A browser session route is not automatically available to partner credentials.

200.description: The new company count and the companies in use

202.description: Sent to Stripe, outcome not recorded yet: `pending_company_quantity` is the count it is moving to and `pending_change_id` identifies the operation. Core reconciles the outcome with Stripe. Operator review may be needed. Until resolved, another change answers 409 COMPANY_QUANTITY_CHANGE_IN_PROGRESS

data.description:
One custom FX window row. Scalars are stringified for stable wire/UI parsing
(decimals keep full precision; timestamps are UTC ISO-8601).

Rate direction: `1 target_currency = exchange_rate base_currency`, where
`base_currency` is the company's base currency. This is the same convention as a
document's `document_exchange_rate` ("1 document currency = X company currency").

effective_from.description:
First instant the window applies (UTC). Start of `effective_from_date` in the
company timezone.

effective_from_date.description:
Company-local calendar date the window starts (`YYYY-MM-DD`). UIs should display
and edit this, not a slice of the UTC timestamp (which can be the previous day).

effective_to.description: Last instant the window applies (UTC, inclusive). `null` = open-ended.

effective_to_date.description: Company-local calendar date the window ends, inclusive (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

data.description: Response for `switch-automatic`: what happened to the pair's current/upcoming windows.

ended_ids.description: Windows that were in effect before today and now end yesterday.

company_quantity.description: The count the plan pays for, as recorded.

payment_url.description: Stripe-hosted invoice for the pending browser payment.

pending_change_id.description: The operation ID for correlating a pending change.

pending_company_quantity.description:
Set (with HTTP 202) when the change was sent to Stripe but its outcome
is not recorded yet: the count it is moving to. Until it settles,
another change answers 409 COMPANY_QUANTITY_CHANGE_IN_PROGRESS, and no
company can be added beyond the lower of the two counts. Unresolved
changes may require operator review.

data.description:
What changing the count would charge now. A decrease charges nothing: its
`total` is negative, the credit for the unused time.

amount_due.description:
What is charged now, after any credit on the Stripe customer, in minor
units (cents).

lines.description:
The preview's invoice lines, so a surprising amount can be explained
(and shown) line by line. Empty when the count is unchanged.

proration_date.description:
Unix seconds the preview prorated to; send it back with the update.
None when the count is unchanged.

total.description:
The change's cost before credit, in minor units; negative for a
decrease (the credit it adds to the balance). Above `amount_due`
when account credit (e.g. the unused part of a replaced subscription)
covers some or all of it, so the client can say so instead of showing
a bare zero.

CurrencyExchangeRateResponse.description: Successful response envelope. Read the operation result from `data`; list metadata belongs inside that result.

as_of_date_matched.description:
`false` when an automatic rate was returned for a date before today: no
historical provider rates are stored, so it is the latest rate, not that day's.

tags.name: Access & Permissions
tags.description:
### Access Control & Authorization

This module manages role-based access control (RBAC) across the platform. It defines how users are authorized to perform actions within a company by assigning roles and permissions.

**Key Capabilities:**
- Create and manage company-specific roles
- Assign granular permissions to roles across modules
- Resolve effective permissions for users
- Enforce tenant-isolated access

**How It Works:**
Each user is associated with a role within a company. Roles contain a set of permissions (e.g., `invoice.create`, `expense.approve`) that determine what actions the user can perform.

All access checks are evaluated dynamically and are scoped per tenant, ensuring strict data isolation and security.

**Use Cases:**
- Define Admin, Accountant, or Viewer roles
- Restrict access to sensitive operations (e.g., financial approvals)
- Enable fine-grained feature control across modules

tags.name: Company / Payment Instructions
tags.description:
### Treasury & Payout Configuration
Endpoints for managing the organization's verified bank accounts and disbursement methods. These instructions serve as the authoritative source for automated payouts, payroll distribution, and bank reconciliation within the accounting engine. 

**Security Note:** All modifications are recorded in the system audit log to maintain fiscal integrity.

tags.name: Company
tags.description:
### Organization Management
Endpoints for creating, updating, and managing company profiles. Includes onboarding workflows, logo management, and soft-delete capabilities.

tags.name: Company / Connections
tags.description:
### Inter-Company Relationships
Management of company-to-company connection mappings, enabling B2B collaboration and document exchange between organizations.

tags.name: Company / Currency
tags.description:
### Multi-Currency Configuration
Endpoints for configuring the currencies supported by the organization, including default currency selection and exchange rate preferences.

tags.name: Company / Email Templates
tags.description:
### Transactional Email Customization
Management of email templates used for automated communications such as invoice delivery, payment reminders, and receipt notifications.

tags.name: Company / Payment Modes
tags.description:
### Accepted Payment Methods
Management of the payment methods (e.g., Bank Transfer, Cash, Cheque) that the organization accepts from its clients.

tags.name: Company / Payment Terms
tags.description:
### Invoice Payment Terms
Configuration of standard payment term templates (e.g., Net 30, Net 60, Due on Receipt) applied to invoices and bills.

tags.name: Company / Email Delivery
tags.description:
### Email Delivery Configuration
Management of SMTP server settings used for sending transactional emails. Supports TLS/SSL security methods and custom server configurations.

tags.name: Company / Stripe Connect
tags.description:
### Stripe Connect Integration
Endpoints for managing Stripe Connect accounts, enabling marketplace-style payment flows with connected account onboarding, status tracking, and account lifecycle management.

tags.name: Organization
tags.description: Run the companies of a Standard organization from your app: list them, read one company's usage or the organization's totals against its plan, add a company, and change or preview how many companies the plan pays for. Call these as the organization company. To work in one of its companies, exchange your App Connect credentials with `member_company_id` for that company's token.

tags.name: Items
tags.description:
### Product & Service Registry

Centralized management of the organization's catalog. This module handles both tangible inventory and intangible services, providing the essential pricing, tax, and accounting metadata required for document line items (Invoices, Bills, and Quotes).

tags.name: Clients
tags.description:
### Customer Relationship Management

Central registry for all revenue-generating entities. This module tracks client profiles, billing addresses, and default payment terms used to automate the generation of **Quotes** and **Invoices**.

tags.name: Vendors
tags.description:
### Supplier & Partner Registry

Management of external service providers and product suppliers. Use these endpoints to maintain procurement contact data, default expense categories, and credit terms for **Bills** and **Purchase Orders**.

tags.name: Invoices
tags.description:
### Accounts Receivable

Formal billing documents issued to clients. Use these endpoints to manage the lifecycle of revenue collection, from draft generation to final payment reconciliation.

tags.name: Quotes
tags.description:
### Sales Proposals

Non-binding estimates and price quotes. These serve as the initial engagement point and can be converted into active Invoices once approved by the customer.

tags.name: Credit Notes
tags.description:
### Revenue Adjustments

Documents issued to reduce a customer's balance. Essential for handling returns, disputes, or overpayments while maintaining an accurate audit trail.

tags.name: Bills
tags.description:
### Accounts Payable

Vendor-issued invoices recorded for internal payment. Use these to track external liabilities and manage outgoing cash flow and supplier settlements.

tags.name: Purchase Orders
tags.description:
### Procurement Control

Official authorization sent to vendors for purchases. POs act as the primary control mechanism for corporate spending and inventory tracking.

tags.name: Expenses
tags.description: Record, inspect, and manage tenant expenses, including line items, taxes, attributes, and supporting attachments.

tags.name: Accounting / Dimensions
tags.description: Generally available accounting dimensions: manage tenant-owned definitions and values, classify transaction lines, report by dimension, and correct missing assignments. Dimensions remain optional; deployment availability and existing permissions apply.

tags.name: Accounting / Journals
tags.description:
### General Ledger & Journal Entries

Create, inspect, and correct the tenant's primary accounting records. Posted journals follow double-entry rules and retain their original audit evidence.

* **Audit Trail:** Every entry generates a unique transaction hash.
* **Versioning:** GET returns the current version plus a short version_history. Pass version to load one earlier version.
* **Corrections:** Posted history is preserved; drafts can still be updated or deleted. Void reverses financial impact without deleting the original record.

tags.name: Accounting / Accounts
tags.description:
### Cash & Liquidity Management

Control and reconciliation of bank accounts, petty cash, and credit lines. Use these endpoints to track real-time balances and synchronize external bank statements with the internal ledger.

tags.name: Accounting / Reconciliations
tags.description:
### Verification & Financial Integrity

The process of matching internal ledger records against external bank statements. This module ensures that the 'Book Balance' and 'Statement Balance' are synchronized.

* **Discrepancy Control:** Automatically calculates the 'diff' to identify missing or erroneous transactions.
* **Transaction Locking:** Finalizing a reconciliation locks the associated period, preventing retrospective changes to the audit trail.
* **Adjustment Journals:** Supports the direct creation of balancing entries for bank charges or interest.

tags.name: Accounting / Transactions
tags.description:
### Ledger Ingestion & Categorization

The foundational layer of the general ledger, handling the intake of all financial movements from linked bank feeds and manual entries.

* **Matching Engine:** Support for linking bank movements to existing Invoices, Bills, and Journal Entries to close the loop on accounts receivable/payable.
* **Exclusion Logic:** Capabilities to 'Ignore' or 'Exclude' non-business movements or duplicates while maintaining a clear audit trail of the reason.
* **Entity Mapping:** Allows for complex 'Many-to-Many' splits, where a single transaction can be allocated across multiple ledger entities.

tags.name: Taxes & Submissions
tags.description:
### Tax Configuration & Reporting

This module manages tax definitions, calculations, and regulatory reporting across the platform. It enables businesses to define applicable taxes, apply them to transactions, and generate structured tax reports for compliance.

**Key Capabilities:**
- Create and manage tax rates (e.g., GST, VAT, Sales Tax)
- Support multiple tax types and categories (sale, purchase, etc.)
- Configure recoverable vs non-recoverable taxes
- Apply taxes dynamically to invoices, expenses, and transactions
- Generate and submit tax reports
- Track tax report submissions and their lifecycle
- Build a tax from reusable components (a US state, county and city stack; an Indian CGST and SGST split), each with its own dated rates

**Tax components:**
A component is a percentage with its own rate history. A tax made of components charges their sum on the line's taxable base, and the line tax is split across them. Fixed-amount levies, compound (tax-on-tax) components and components on a different base are not supported. Rate classes are separate components. Codes are free identifiers, unique per company and matched exactly after trimming; `country_code` and `region` are optional and checked for ISO format and prefix only.

**How It Works:**
Taxes are defined at the company (tenant) level and linked to financial transactions. Each tax includes attributes such as rate, category, and recoverability.

During transaction processing, applicable taxes are calculated and stored. These records are later aggregated into tax reports, which can be submitted and tracked via the reporting workflow.

**Use Cases:**
- Configure GST/VAT for invoices and expenses
- Handle input/output tax tracking for compliance
- Generate periodic tax reports (monthly, quarterly, etc.)
- Maintain audit-ready tax submission records

tags.name: Audit Activity
tags.description:
### Operational Audit Trail & Record History

A high-fidelity registry of all system interactions and data mutations. This module provides a centralized, immutable timeline of 'Who, What, and When,' ensuring total transparency across the organization. It tracks the complete evolution of records—from initial creation to final archival—offering the forensic evidence required for internal oversight and regulatory compliance.

tags.name: Late Fees
tags.description:
### Invoice Late Fee Rules
Endpoints for managing the penalty rules applied to overdue invoices. Use these APIs to define percentage-based or flat late fee policies, control activation, and retrieve the rules available to a company for document workflows.

tags.name: Projects & Timesheets
tags.description:
### Project Management
Endpoints for managing projects, reusable tasks, and billable timesheets within the authenticated company. Use these APIs to maintain project work, log time, and retrieve invoice-ready time summaries.
